title: The Village Idiot
summary: A village boy always chooses a shiny copper coin over a dull silver coin. Akbar thinks the boy is a fool, but Birbal reveals the boy's genius.
full_text:
While traveling through a village on the road to Gwalior, Emperor Akbar was told by the local villagers about a young boy named Sukhi, whom everyone called the 'village idiot.'

The village headman laughed: 'Your Majesty, this boy has no brain at all! Every day, travelers hold out a large, shiny copper coin in one hand, and a small, dull silver coin in the other, and tell him to choose. The fool always picks the copper coin, and everyone laughs!'

Curious, Akbar called the boy over. In his right palm, Akbar placed a small, polished silver rupee. In his left palm, he placed a large, broad copper dam.

Akbar said: 'Sukhi, take whichever coin you want; it is yours.'

Sukhi looked at both coins with wide, innocent eyes, picked the large copper coin, gave a silly grin, and hopped away happily!

Akbar chuckled: 'Truly, the poor boy does not know the value of metals! A silver coin is worth thirty copper dams, yet he chooses the copper because it is bigger!'

Birbal walked over to the shade of a tamarind tree where Sukhi was sitting alone. Birbal smiled kindly and asked in a low voice: 'Sukhi, you are an observant boy. Do you truly not know that a silver coin can buy thirty times more sweets than a copper coin?'

Sukhi looked around, made sure no villagers were listening, and whispered with a mischievous grin:

'Of course I know that, wise minister! I am not a fool!'

Birbal raised his eyebrows: 'Then why do you always pick the copper coin?'

Sukhi chuckled softly:

'My lord, if I pick the silver coin just once, the travelers and villagers will realize that I know the difference, and the game will end forever!

'By picking the copper coin every day, they believe I am an idiot, so every day fifty new travelers line up to test me, and I walk home every evening with fifty copper coins in my pocket! Why should I take one silver coin today and lose fifty copper coins tomorrow?'

Birbal laughed with pure delight. He brought the boy back to Akbar and shared Sukhi's confession.

Akbar stared in astonishment, then laughed till his sides ached: 'By Allah, Birbal! The boy is smarter than half my imperial council! He lets the world call him a fool while he quietly gathers the harvest of their arrogance!'

Akbar rewarded Sukhi with a purse of silver, warning him to keep his secret safe.
moral: நீதி மற்றும் வாழ்க்கை பாடம்: Wit beats power
